summary: 50-year-old hiker fell 40 ft at 14,020 ft below Mt Sneffels summit (Lavender Couloir area); head injury, broken leg, severe hypothermia; OMRT bivouacked with him through violent weather and a National Guard helicopter hoisted him out the next morning
location: Mt Sneffels, below summit / Lavender Couloir
responding_agency: Ouray Mountain Rescue Team + Army National Guard helicopter
notes: CSAR award-winning rescue; second source is a long-form narrative of the same mission | Rocky Talkie/AAC SAR Award story adds detail: volunteer responders Grant Kleeves, OMRT Lt. Patrick Brighton, Capt. Ruth Stewart; dispatch mixed signals ("confirmed fatality" then "cancel"); 2 in. hail, sustained lightning, sub-20F temps pinning teams at vehicles; mudslide took out the road, cleared by a local miner's bulldozer; patient combative from head injury + hypothermia ("paradoxical undressing"); team bivouacked overnight on the summit ledge; National Guard helo hoist at dawn. | Road-clearing miner named in the CSAR Valor Award account as Bumper Williams (hard-rock miner who heard radio traffic and used mine heavy equipment to clear the washed-out road to the trailhead).
